Notes: Sociopolitical Chamber (80 seats) of Assembly of Socialist Republic of Slovenia; first multi-party election; pre-independence.
First election to independent Slovenia's National Assembly (Državni zbor); 90 seats including 2 minority MPs.
Second post-independence election to the National Assembly.
Joint SLS–SKD list (SLS-SKD) won 9 seats; breakdown by party not available in standard sources.
First regular election after EU accession (2004).
SD wins plurality; coalition with Zares, LDS and DeSUS.
Early election; new party Positive Slovenia (PS) wins plurality.
SMC (Miro Cerar) landslide; United Left (ZL) enters parliament; SLS and PS lose representation.
Fragmented parliament; LMŠ, Levica and SAB gain seats.
Freedom Movement (GS) wins 41 seats; centre-left government formed under Robert Golob.
